# Source: README.md

# Hero

Hero is the shared Rust library for the Midwess organization. It provides the
small, reusable patterns used by Midwess services, workers, native
applications, and browser/WASM clients at architectural boundaries.

Hero is intentionally not a framework. It does not own application domains,
databases, local storage, dependency-injection containers, or generic service
layers. It focuses on cancellation, resource pooling, identifiers, gateway
registration, network listeners, object storage, mail delivery, tokens,
logging, and browser integration.

Every capability is opt-in. The default feature set is empty, and a no-feature
build enables no normal dependency.

## Installation

Until a license and publication policy are selected, consume Hero by pinned
Git revision:

```toml
[dependencies]
hero = {
    git = "ssh://git@github.com/Midwess/hero.git",
    rev = "<commit>",
    features = ["cancellation", "task"]
}
```

Do not use `all-features` in an application dependency. Start with no features,
then add only the capabilities the application imports.

## Architectural Role

Keep business rules in the consuming application's domain and application
layers. Use Hero at infrastructure boundaries and in shared runtime code:

- propagate cancellation through nested asynchronous work;
- pool and automatically return reusable infrastructure resources;
- allocate IDs in one process or across an etcd-coordinated fleet;
- bind service listeners and register routes with the Midwess Kong gateway;
- connect tonic clients through the shared gRPC gateway;
- interact with S3-compatible storage and SMTP infrastructure;
- issue and validate JWTs at authentication boundaries;
- normalize logging, environments, retries, and task cleanup;
- expose browser HTTP, byte conversion, and OPFS helpers to WASM clients.

Product schemas, repositories, business entities, and product-specific
orchestration belong in the consuming application or a separate library.

## Common Combinations

The minimum column assumes the component uses every Hero capability named in
the scenario. Optional additions are conventions, not transitive requirements.

| Scenario | Minimum features | Optional additions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hero-managed TCP listener and Kong registration for an HTTP service | `api-gateway`, `tcp` | `config`, `logger`, `cancellation` when imported |
| Hero-managed gRPC listener and Kong registration | `api-gateway`, `grpc-server` | `config`, `logger`, `cancellation` when imported |
| Client calling services through Kong | `grpc-gateway` | `logger`, `cancellation` when imported |
| Worker using cancellation, owned tasks, and retry | `cancellation`, `task`, `retry` | `logger` |
| Fleet-wide ID producer | `distributed-id-etcd` | `logger` |
| Single-process ID producer | `distributed-id` | None |
| Backend using object storage | `s3` | `logger`, `retry` when imported |
| Backend sending rendered email | `smtp` | `logger`, `retry`, `task` when imported |
| Reusable infrastructure resource pool | `pool` | None |
| Browser HTTP/OPFS client | `wasm` | `cancellation`, `stream`, `time`, `logger` when imported |

If the application framework already binds its listener, omit
`tcp`/`grpc-server`. If route registration is handled by deployment tooling,
omit `api-gateway`. Add `config` only when importing `hero::config`.

## Feature Index

Feature names use kebab-case. Rust module names use snake_case. Select a feature
for details, exact API paths, environment variables, and related capabilities.

| Feature | API root | Target | Implies | Introduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`api-gateway`](docs/features/api-gateway.md) | `hero::api_gateway` | Native | None | Define and register Kong services, routes, and plugins. |
| [`cancellation`](docs/features/cancellation.md) | `hero::cancellation` | Native/WASM | None | Propagate structured, scoped cancellation through async work. |
| [`config`](docs/features/config.md) | `hero::config` | Native/WASM | None | Read the standard Midwess Kong and environment configuration. |
| [`distributed-id`](docs/features/distributed-id.md) | `hero::distributed_id` | Native/WASM | None | Generate Snowflake-style IDs without a coordinator. |
| [`distributed-id-etcd`](docs/features/distributed-id-etcd.md) | `hero::distributed_id` | Native | `distributed-id` | Coordinate distributed-ID worker leases through etcd. |
| [`env`](docs/features/env.md) | `hero::env` | Native/WASM | None | Normalize local, development, staging, and production checks. |
| [`finally`](docs/features/finally.md) | `hero::finally` | Native/WASM | None | Run collected asynchronous cleanup work when an owner drops. |
| [`grpc-gateway`](docs/features/grpc-gateway.md) | `hero::grpc_gateway` | Native | `config` | Reuse a tonic channel through the configured gateway. |
| [`grpc-server`](docs/features/grpc-server.md) | `hero::tcp::listener` | Native | `tcp` | Add tonic incoming-listener support to Hero's TCP pattern. |
| [`logger`](docs/features/logger.md) | `hero::logger` | Native/WASM | None | Apply Midwess logging defaults and throttled logging. |
| [`maybe`](docs/features/maybe.md) | `hero::maybe` | Native/WASM | None | Express target-dependent sendability in generic APIs. |
| [`never-send`](docs/features/never-send.md) | `hero::never_send` | Native/WASM | None | Mark a value as intentionally local without faking auto-traits. |
| [`number`](docs/features/number.md) | `hero::number` | Native/WASM | None | Compute time-based exponential integer growth. |
| [`pool`](docs/features/pool.md) | `hero::pool` | Native/WASM | `maybe` | Manage bounded reusable resources and waiter queues. |
| [`retry`](docs/features/retry.md) | `hero::retry` | Native/WASM | None | Retry transient async operations with fixed or capped backoff. |
| [`s3`](docs/features/s3.md) | `hero::s3` | Native | None | Access S3-compatible object storage with product-neutral paths. |
| [`shell`](docs/features/shell.md) | `hero::shell` | Native | None | Consume piped child stdout and stderr as one async stream. |
| [`smtp`](docs/features/smtp.md) | `hero::smtp` | Native | `cancellation` | Send rendered HTML email with delivery cancellation. |
| [`stream`](docs/features/stream.md) | `hero::stream` | Native/WASM | None | Create in-memory duplex byte streams. |
| [`string`](docs/features/string.md) | `hero::string` | Native/WASM | None | Use shared string validation helpers. |
| [`task`](docs/features/task.md) | `hero::task` | Native | None | Abort an owned Tokio task when its guard drops. |
| [`tcp`](docs/features/tcp.md) | `hero::tcp` | Native | None | Bind dual-stack TCP/UDP listeners without tonic. |
| [`throttle-future`](docs/features/throttle-future.md) | `hero::throttle_future` | Native/WASM | None | Coalesce frequent values before asynchronous processing. |
| [`time`](docs/features/time.md) | `hero::time` | Native/WASM | None | Read epoch time in microseconds across targets. |
| [`token`](docs/features/token.md) | `hero::token` | Native | None | Create and decode HS256 JSON Web Tokens. |
| [`wasm`](docs/features/wasm.md) | `hero::wasm` | WASM | None | Use browser HTTP, byte/file, and OPFS helpers. |
| [`yield-container`](docs/features/yield-container.md) | `hero::yield_container` | Native/WASM | None | Lend a value temporarily and return it on drop. |

These entries are introductions, not bundled presets. List individual features
in the consuming `Cargo.toml` so architectural dependencies remain visible.

## What Hero Does Not Include

Hero deliberately excludes:

- database repositories and persistence abstractions;
- local filesystem/storage orchestration and ZIP packaging;
- a generic application service trait or catch-all error type;
- product schemas, protobuf-generated domain types, and Crafter templates;
- application dependency-injection containers;
- business workflows and product-specific policy.

See [MIGRATION.md](MIGRATION.md) when moving from `core-services` or
`devlog-sdk`. See [HISTORY.md](HISTORY.md) for imported repository history.

## Documentation

- [Feature documentation](docs/features/README.md)
- [Migration guide](MIGRATION.md)
- [Source history](HISTORY.md)
- [Documentation publishing](docs/publishing.md)

## Development

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --all-features
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
scripts/check-features.sh
scripts/check-exclusions.sh
scripts/check-docs.sh
scripts/build-docs-bundle.sh
```

The validation scripts keep Hero flat, opt-in, documented, and independently
buildable by feature on supported native and WASM targets.

---

# Source: AGENTS.md

# Hero Repository Instructions

Before modifying Hero, read these files in order:

1. `llms.txt`
2. `hero.features.json`
3. the relevant page under `docs/features/`
4. `Cargo.toml`

Repository invariants:

- `default = []` must remain empty.
- Every public module must have an explicit Cargo feature.
- Every normal dependency must be optional and owned by a feature.
- Do not reintroduce `utils`, `db`, `local_storage`, `services`, or `sdk` modules.
- Do not add broad production presets such as `full` or `backend`.
- Native-only features must remain unavailable on WASM.
- Feature relationships belong in `Cargo.toml` and `hero.features.json`.
- Keep README content product-facing; discovery-system instructions belong in
  `llms.txt`, `AGENTS.md`, and `docs/indexing.md`.

When adding or changing a feature:

1. Update `Cargo.toml`.
2. Update `hero.features.json`.
3. Run `node scripts/generate-feature-docs.mjs`.
4. Update source and tests.
5. Run `scripts/check-docs.sh`, `scripts/check-features.sh`, and
   `scripts/check-exclusions.sh`.
6. Run native and supported-WASM Clippy checks.

---

# Source: docs/architecture.md

# Hero Architecture

Hero provides reusable infrastructure and runtime patterns for the Midwess
organization. It sits between application code and external/runtime boundaries.

## Principles

### Explicit capabilities

Hero has an empty default feature set. A consumer's `Cargo.toml` records the
architectural capabilities it uses. A feature owns its dependencies and may
imply only features required by its implementation.

### Flat public modules

Public modules are available directly below `hero`. There is no generic
`utils` namespace. Feature names use kebab-case and module names use
snake_case.

### Domain independence

Hero accepts product-neutral values at infrastructure boundaries. Product
schemas, protobuf adapters, repositories, and business policy remain in the
consumer or a separate domain library.

### Local errors

Integrations own their error types. Hero does not define a catch-all service
error or generic application service abstraction.

### Target isolation

Native and WASM dependencies are isolated. Native-only features expose no
module on browser targets. Cross-platform features are validated independently
on both targets.

## Common Flows

### Service ingress

1. Bind a listener with `tcp` or `grpc-server` when Hero owns listener setup.
2. Build Kong routes with `api-gateway` when the process owns registration.
3. Add `config`, `logger`, and `cancellation` only when those modules are used.

### Service client

1. Enable `grpc-gateway`.
2. The feature enables `config` for gateway endpoint discovery.
3. Reuse `GrpcGatewayChannel` instead of rebuilding tonic channels per call.

### Distributed identity

1. Use `distributed-id` for one process or explicitly assigned worker IDs.
2. Use `distributed-id-etcd` when worker IDs require fleet coordination.
3. Explicitly shut down etcd-backed generation to revoke the lease.

### Owned asynchronous work

Compose `cancellation`, `task`, `retry`, `finally`, and `yield-container`
according to the ownership and shutdown behavior required by the component.

---

# Source: docs/features/README.md

# Hero Feature Documentation

Hero has an empty default feature set. Select only the capabilities imported by
the consuming project.

| Feature | API root | Target | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`api-gateway`](api-gateway.md) | `hero::api_gateway` | Native | Define and register Kong services, routes, and plugins. |
| [`cancellation`](cancellation.md) | `hero::cancellation` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Propagate structured, scoped cancellation through async work. |
| [`config`](config.md) | `hero::config` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Read the standard Midwess Kong and deployment configuration. |
| [`distributed-id`](distributed-id.md) | `hero::distributed_id` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Generate Snowflake-style IDs without a coordination service. |
| [`distributed-id-etcd`](distributed-id-etcd.md) | `hero::distributed_id` | Native | Coordinate distributed-ID worker leases through etcd. |
| [`env`](env.md) | `hero::env` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Normalize local, development, staging, and production checks. |
| [`finally`](finally.md) | `hero::finally` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Run collected asynchronous cleanup work when an owner drops. |
| [`grpc-gateway`](grpc-gateway.md) | `hero::grpc_gateway` | Native | Reuse a tonic channel through the configured gateway. |
| [`grpc-server`](grpc-server.md) | `hero::tcp::listener` | Native | Add tonic incoming-listener support to Hero's TCP pattern. |
| [`logger`](logger.md) | `hero::logger` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Apply Midwess logging defaults and throttled logging. |
| [`maybe`](maybe.md) | `hero::maybe` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Express target-dependent sendability in generic APIs. |
| [`never-send`](never-send.md) | `hero::never_send` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Mark a value as intentionally local without faking auto-traits. |
| [`number`](number.md) | `hero::number` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Compute time-based exponential integer growth. |
| [`pool`](pool.md) | `hero::pool` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Manage bounded reusable resources and waiter queues. |
| [`retry`](retry.md) | `hero::retry` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Retry transient async operations with fixed or capped backoff. |
| [`s3`](s3.md) | `hero::s3` | Native | Access S3-compatible object storage with product-neutral paths. |
| [`shell`](shell.md) | `hero::shell` | Native | Consume piped child stdout and stderr as one async stream. |
| [`smtp`](smtp.md) | `hero::smtp` | Native | Send rendered HTML email with delivery cancellation. |
| [`stream`](stream.md) | `hero::stream` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Create in-memory duplex byte streams. |
| [`string`](string.md) | `hero::string` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Use shared string validation helpers. |
| [`task`](task.md) | `hero::task` | Native | Abort an owned Tokio task when its guard drops. |
| [`tcp`](tcp.md) | `hero::tcp` | Native | Bind dual-stack TCP and UDP listeners without tonic. |
| [`throttle-future`](throttle-future.md) | `hero::throttle_future` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Coalesce frequent values before asynchronous processing. |
| [`time`](time.md) | `hero::time` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Read epoch time in microseconds across targets. |
| [`token`](token.md) | `hero::token` | Native | Create and decode HS256 JSON Web Tokens. |
| [`wasm`](wasm.md) | `hero::wasm` | `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Use browser HTTP, byte/file, and OPFS helpers. |
| [`yield-container`](yield-container.md) | `hero::yield_container` | Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` | Lend a value temporarily and return it on drop. |

The machine-readable equivalent is [`hero.features.json`](../../hero.features.json).
The executable feature graph is [`Cargo.toml`](../../Cargo.toml).

# api-gateway

Define and register Kong services, routes, and plugins.

## Enable

```toml
[dependencies]
hero = {
    git = "ssh://git@github.com/Midwess/hero.git",
    rev = "<commit>",
    features = ["api-gateway"]
}
```

## Availability

- API root: `hero::api_gateway`
- Target: Native
- Implied Hero features: None

## Enable When

- The process constructs Kong route definitions.
- The process registers or removes services through the Kong Admin API.

## Primary APIs

- `hero::api_gateway::service::GatewayServiceBuilder`
- `hero::api_gateway::service::GatewayRouteBuilder`
- `hero::api_gateway::client::ApiGatewayClient`
- `hero::api_gateway::kong::client::KongGatewayAdminClient`

## Import Example

```rust,no_run
use hero::api_gateway::service::GatewayServiceBuilder;
```

## Environment

This feature does not define environment variables.

## Selection Notes

- Hero's default feature set is empty.
- Enable `api-gateway` only when the consuming code uses this capability.
- Features listed under "Implied Hero features" are enabled automatically by Cargo.
- Validate the consuming project's actual target after changing its feature list.

## Related Documentation

- [Feature index](README.md)
- [Hero overview](../../README.md)
- [Machine-readable catalog](../../hero.features.json)
- [Migration guide](../../MIGRATION.md)

# never-send

Mark a value as intentionally local without faking auto-traits.

## Enable

```toml
[dependencies]
hero = {
    git = "ssh://git@github.com/Midwess/hero.git",
    rev = "<commit>",

}
```

## Availability

- API root: `hero::never_send`
- Target: Native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- Implied Hero features: None

## Enable When

- A wrapper should communicate thread-local ownership.

## Primary APIs

- `hero::never_send::NeverSend`

## Import Example

```rust,no_run
use hero::never_send::NeverSend;
```

## Environment

This feature does not define environment variables.

## Selection Notes

- Hero's default feature set is empty.
- Enable `never-send` only when the consuming code uses this capability.
- Features listed under "Implied Hero features" are enabled automatically by Cargo.
- Validate the consuming project's actual target after changing its feature list.

## Related Documentation

- [Feature index](README.md)
- [Hero overview](../../README.md)
- [Machine-readable catalog](../../hero.features.json)
- [Migration guide](../../MIGRATION.md)

# Source: MIGRATION.md

# Migrating to Hero

Hero replaces the retained capabilities of `core-services` and `devlog-sdk`.
It is intentionally a breaking, fully opt-in migration with no default
features and no legacy module or feature aliases.

## Dependency

Replace both old dependencies with one Hero dependency and the union of the
retained features that the application uses:

```toml
# Before
core-services = { path = "../core-services", features = ["grpc-server"] }
devlog-sdk = { path = "../devlog-sdk", features = ["gateway", "tcp"] }

# After
hero = { path = "../hero", features = ["grpc-server", "api-gateway"] }
```

## Import Prefixes

Retained modules stay at the top level:

```text
core_services::utils::cancellation     -> hero::cancellation
core_services::utils::finally          -> hero::finally
core_services::utils::maybe            -> hero::maybe
core_services::utils::never_send       -> hero::never_send
core_services::utils::number           -> hero::number
core_services::utils::pool             -> hero::pool
core_services::utils::stream           -> hero::stream
core_services::utils::string           -> hero::string
core_services::utils::throttle_future  -> hero::throttle_future
core_services::utils::time             -> hero::time
core_services::utils::yield_container  -> hero::yield_container
core_services::logger         -> hero::logger
core_services::env            -> hero::env
core_services::s3             -> hero::s3
core_services::smtp           -> hero::smtp
core_services::token          -> hero::token
core_services::shell          -> hero::shell
core_services::wasm           -> hero::wasm

devlog_sdk::api_gateway       -> hero::api_gateway
devlog_sdk::config            -> hero::config
devlog_sdk::distributed_id    -> hero::distributed_id
devlog_sdk::grpc_gateway      -> hero::grpc_gateway
devlog_sdk::retry             -> hero::retry
devlog_sdk::task              -> hero::task
devlog_sdk::tcp               -> hero::tcp
```

## Removed Capabilities

Hero has no replacement for:

- `core_services::db`
- `core_services::local_storage`
- the generic `core_services::services::Service` abstraction

Move those capabilities into application-owned code or a dedicated library.
Retained Kong, TCP, S3, and SMTP APIs now expose errors in their own modules
instead of using `services::Errors`.

Hero also removes:

- `devlog_sdk::sdk::DevlogSdk`
- `devlog_sdk::sdk::DependenciesInjection`

Use `hero::s3::S3Config::from_env()?.build_client()` where an S3 client is
needed. Consumers that constructed an empty `DevlogSdk` can remove it.

## Feature Changes

| Old feature | Hero replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `host_machine` | `shell` |
| `distributed_id` | `distributed-id-etcd` |
| `gateway` | `api-gateway` |
| `grpc-client` | `grpc-gateway` |
| `backend` | Select every required capability individually |
| `db-red` | Removed |
| `db-idb` | Removed |
| `local-storage` | Removed |
| `zip` | Removed |
| `zstd` | Removed |
| `services` | Removed |

The previous default exports are now feature-gated. For example, using
`hero::cancellation` requires `features = ["cancellation"]`, and using the
pool requires `features = ["pool"]`. Cross-module requirements are encoded in
Cargo: `smtp` enables `cancellation`, `pool` enables `maybe`, `grpc-server`
enables `tcp`, and `distributed-id-etcd` enables `distributed-id`.

## API Changes

### Gateway builders

`GatewayRouteBuilder::build` and `GatewayServiceBuilder::build` now return
`Result` instead of panicking when required fields are missing.

### Distributed IDs

- Prefer `try_gen_id` and native `try_gen_id_sync`.
- `id_to_datetime` now returns `Result`.
- Scoped and etcd initialization report duplicate initialization.
- Call `shutdown_id_generator().await` before native etcd-backed shutdown.

The old `gen_id` functions remain deprecated panic-based wrappers for a short
source migration window.

### S3

- Schema protobuf types are replaced by `hero::s3::ObjectPath`.
- Environment parsing is handled by `S3Config::from_env`.
- Access to the underlying AWS client is read-only through `raw_client`.

Product-specific `StaticResource` conversions belong in the consuming
application or a separate adapter crate.

### SMTP

`SmtpClient::send_html` accepts a rendered subject and HTML body. Crafter and
product protobuf rendering are no longer library responsibilities.

### Pooling

- `pool::reponse` is removed; use `pool::response`.
- `PoolResourceProvider::new` is renamed to `create`.
- `PoolBuilder::build` and `PoolRequestBuilder::build` return `Result`.
- `NeverSend<T>` no longer unsafely implements `Send` or `Sync`.
- `NeverSend<T>` no longer provides implicit Serde forwarding; serialize the
  wrapped value explicitly when needed.

### Shell and gRPC

- Construct `StdStream` with `TryFrom<tokio::process::Child>`.
- `GrpcGatewayChannel::new` returns `Result`.
- `connect_with_timeout` returns the connected channel.

### Browser extensions

`VecExtension` methods are renamed to `to_uint8_array`, `to_js_value`, and
unsafe `view_uint8_array`. JSON bodies and missing URLs now return errors.

---

# Source: HISTORY.md

# Source History

Hero preserves the complete Git histories of its two source libraries as
ancestors of the Hero main branch.

| Source | Repository | Imported tip |
| --- | --- | --- |

The final source tree is a scoped consolidation, not a complete union. The
former `db`, `local_storage`, `services`, and SDK facade modules are excluded.

# Source: docs/indexing.md

# Documentation Indexing Guidance

This document defines how Hero documentation should be ingested by approved
search, retrieval, coding, and documentation systems.

## Canonical Inputs

Use these sources in priority order:

1. `Cargo.toml` for the executable feature graph and dependency truth.
2. `hero.features.json` for machine-readable selection metadata.
3. `docs/features/<feature>.md` for focused feature guidance.
4. rustdoc for item-level signatures and type documentation.
5. `README.md`, `MIGRATION.md`, and `docs/architecture.md` for broader context.

## Chunking

- Treat each feature page as one primary retrieval unit.
- Split rustdoc by public item or module, preserving the fully qualified path.
- Keep feature name, API root, target, implied features, crate version, and Git
  revision as metadata on every chunk.
- Keep migration content in a separate collection from current API guidance.
- Do not merge multiple feature pages into one undifferentiated chunk.

## Versioning

- Index documentation by both Cargo version and full Git revision.
- Never overwrite an indexed released revision with documentation from another
  revision.
- Prefer the bundle metadata produced by `scripts/build-docs-bundle.sh`.
- For an unreleased dependency pinned by `rev`, retrieve documentation with the
  same Git revision.

## Access

- Private repositories require an organization-approved Git provider
  connection, documentation crawler, or MCP server.
- Do not copy private source or documentation into an external provider without
  an approved data-handling agreement.
- Apply repository access controls to the generated documentation bundle and
  any derived vector/search index.

## Retrieval Behavior

- Resolve a requested Rust path using this deterministic order:
  1. exact match against `primary_apis`;
  2. longest matching `api_root` prefix;
  3. if multiple features share that root, return every candidate rather than
     guessing, then use exact item/rustdoc evidence to select an extension.
- Treat features that imply another feature and share/extend its API root as
  capability extensions. Examples are `distributed-id-etcd` over
  `distributed-id` and `grpc-server` over `tcp`.
- Compute the transitive closure of `implies` before presenting the final Cargo
  feature set, but show which features were requested and which were implied.
- For natural-language queries, rank `enable_when`, then `summary`, then
  `primary_apis`; return multiple candidates when scores are close.
- Return target restrictions and implied features with API guidance.
- Prefer minimal feature recommendations over broad feature sets.
- If documentation and Cargo metadata disagree, report the inconsistency and
  treat `Cargo.toml` as authoritative.

# Source: docs/mcp-resource-contract.md

# Hero MCP Resource Contract

An internal documentation MCP server can expose the versioned Hero bundle with
these resource shapes. The URI scheme is illustrative but stable within the
organization once adopted.

| Resource | MIME type | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hero://<revision>/index` | `text/markdown` | Documentation index and architecture links. |
| `hero://<revision>/features` | `application/json` | `hero.features.json`. |
| `hero://<revision>/features/schema` | `application/schema+json` | Feature catalog JSON schema. |
| `hero://<revision>/features/<name>` | `text/markdown` | One focused feature page. |
| `hero://<revision>/manifest` | `text/plain` | The authoritative `Cargo.toml`. |
| `hero://<revision>/bundle-metadata` | `application/json` | Exact bundle version, revision, creation time, and distributable state. |
| `hero://<revision>/rustdoc/native/<path>` | `text/html` | Native rustdoc page. |
| `hero://<revision>/rustdoc/wasm/<path>` | `text/html` | WASM rustdoc page. |
| `hero://<revision>/migration` | `text/markdown` | Migration guide. |
| `hero://<revision>/llms` | `text/plain` | `llms.txt`. |
| `hero://<revision>/llms-full` | `text/plain` | Consolidated documentation corpus. |

## Required Metadata

Every response should include:

- crate name and Cargo version;
- full Git revision;
- target, when applicable;
- feature name and implied features, when applicable;
- source path within the bundle;
- bundle creation time.

The manifest, feature catalog, catalog schema, and bundle metadata resources
must be retrievable directly so clients can verify feature and revision claims.

## Query Guidance

The server should support listing feature resources and retrieving one resource
without requiring the complete corpus. Search results should preserve feature
and target metadata so callers can recommend minimal valid feature sets.
API-path lookup should follow the exact-item, longest-prefix, and ambiguity
rules in `docs/indexing.md`.

---

# Source: docs/publishing.md

# Publishing Hero Documentation

Hero documentation is built as a versioned artifact and is not automatically
published to a public site.

## Build

```bash
scripts/build-docs-bundle.sh
```

The script validates generated documentation, builds native and supported-WASM
rustdoc, records the Cargo version and Git revision, and creates a compressed
bundle under `target/docs-bundle/`.

## Bundle Contents

- overview, architecture, migration, and history documents;
- `Cargo.toml` and repository operating instructions;
- `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`;
- `hero.features.json` and its schema;
- one page per feature;
- native rustdoc;
- WASM rustdoc for the supported cross-platform feature set;
- `bundle-metadata.json` with the exact version, revision, creation time, and
  distributable state.

## Distribution

The CI workflow uploads the bundle as a repository-controlled build artifact.
Its visibility follows repository and Actions permissions; it is not private if
those permissions are public or broadly shared. The workflow refuses to upload
documentation from a public repository.

Distributable bundles require a clean Git worktree. For local preview only,
`ALLOW_DIRTY_DOCS=1 scripts/build-docs-bundle.sh` creates a bundle marked
`distributable: false`; do not upload or index that preview artifact.

An approved internal documentation site, Git provider connector, search
service, or MCP server can ingest a distributable artifact without rebuilding
documentation.

Before publishing outside the organization, confirm:

- repository visibility and source-code disclosure policy;
- selected license and documentation redistribution rights;
- provider data-retention and training controls;
- authentication and authorization for private documentation;
- revision retention and removal policy.

`AGENTS.md` is included as internal repository operating guidance. Treat it as
organization-internal material unless an explicit publication review approves
it for a broader audience.
